steps.prompt: $473 = 11 \times 43$. Work out $4 - 7 + 3$. Try it on $572$ too. What do you notice?

cards.title: Six: two tests together
cards.body: $6 = 2 \times 3$. A number divides by $6$ when it is even and its digit sum divides by $3$. $714$: even, and $7 + 1 + 4 = 12$, so yes.

steps.text: Alternate the signs: first $-$ second $+$ third.
The alternating sum is $0$, which divides by $11$, so $583$ does too: $583 = 11 \times 53$.

cards.title: Why the 11 test works
cards.body: $10 = 11 - 1$ and $100 = 99 + 1$. So $100x + 10y + z$ is a multiple of $11$ plus $x - y + z$. The remainder by $11$ comes from the alternating sum.

prompts: Which divisibility test do you find most surprising, and why does it work?
